The Hyperparameters That an Outer Method Estimates

Source: R/outer.R
outer_hyper_index.Rd

Returns one row per hyperparameter of a penalized term that is fitted in the joint system, with the link that carries it onto the whole line.

Usage

outer_hyper_index(spec, blocks)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec().

blocks

The block split, as statmod_blocks() returns it.

Value

A data frame with one row per estimated hyperparameter, or per group of shared ones, and three character columns, parameter, term and name. The links that carry each onto the whole line are in the "links" attribute, a list with one element per row of the frame (a list column would not survive the subsetting that the search does). The "members" attribute is a data frame of the same three columns plus row, which lists the hyperparameters that each row represents.

Details

A term whose penalty has a kink is left out. Its coefficients are estimated by a coordinate descent while everything else is held fixed, and the criterion is a Laplace approximation, which needs a second derivative that does not exist at a kink. Those hyperparameters are chosen by a path instead.

A hyperparameter that its own term holds is left out too, whatever the kind of penalty to which it belongs, and so is every member of a shared label when one member holds it.

The result is the index of the hyperparameters on the outer search. The search also moves the coefficients that the criterion estimates (see marginal_coords()), so its dimension is the number of rows plus the number of those coefficients. If there are no rows and no such coefficients, the criterion does not run.

Shared hyperparameters

Hyperparameters carrying the same label through modelterms7::term_ids() are estimated at one value, so they occupy one row: the search has one coordinate for the group. The row is identified by its first member, so that every lookup that reads parameter, term and name keeps working, and the "members" attribute lists the hyperparameters that the row represents.

Sharing does not merge the penalties, which remain two objects estimated at one value, so the derivative of the row is the sum of the derivatives of its members and the value is written back under the key of each member. If no hyperparameter is shared, the member table is the index itself, one line per row.

Two members must carry the same link, since one free value has to lie in both of their domains, and a label may not span a smooth penalty and a kinked one, which are estimated by two different procedures and would be given two different values. Both cases are rejected here, where both sides are visible.

See also

hyper_to_eta() for the map that those links define, statmod_held_ids() for the shared labels that a term holds, index_members() for the member table.
